subject: Request: Backcompat exemption for SDK v3 deprecation
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@sageworks.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Backcompat exemption for SDK v3 deprecation

Hi Hannah (and team),

Quick background: we rely on Redwood SDK v3 in two of our connectors (SageTransform and SageSearch). We saw the deprecation notice for v3 scheduled for 2027-01-15 and that would break our GA customers unless we ship a migration before then. Our migration work is larger than anticipated because of embedded custom serializers and an internal fork of the retry layer.

Ask: would Redwood consider a short-term backcompat exemption / grace period for the v3 REST endpoints for SageWorks customers while we finalize the v4 migration? Specifically, a 90-day extension on deprecation for our account (SageWorks / DEAL-4721) would give us the runway to finish the refactor and test across our enterprise customers.

We've attached a brief compatibility impact matrix that shows affected endpoints and estimated engineering effort. Happy to hop on a quick call with product/infra to review constraints.

Thanks,
Sarah Kim
Head of Integrations, SageWorks
---
Attachment: compat-impact-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Backcompat exemption for SDK v3 deprecation

Team — looping you in. Sarah's asked for a 90-day exemption for SageWorks due to a larger-than-expected migration surface. Attachments are included. Can we confirm:

- feasibility from runtime/infra (Marcus) — can we keep v3 endpoints available for a single customer without hurting rollout?
- product constraints and precedent (Vanessa) — do we have a policy for per-account exemptions?
- legal/procurement gating (Priyom) — any contract implications or SLA concerns if we keep both versions live longer?

I'd like to get a proposed reply to Sarah by EOD tomorrow. If we need a short cross-functional call, I can schedule.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Backcompat exemption for SDK v3 deprecation

Quick read and proposal — I reviewed Sarah's matrix. Thoughts below: 

1) Short-term approach (recommended): approve a 60-day account-level grace period (instead of 90) conditioned on the partner signing a one-off addendum that:
   - commits to a target migration date (we'll propose 2027-03-15),
   - allows Redwood to schedule a forced cut with 14 days notice if platform stability is impacted,
   - accepts that v3 metrics will be retained for 30 days only.

2) Tech feasibility: Marcus confirms infra can route SageWorks traffic to a compatibility cluster with a modest ops cost (approx 2x token-serving overhead for the cohort). We'll require a feature-flag toggle and a short maintenance window to enable the cluster.

3) Risk/precedent: We should log this as an exception in the Partner Playbook and cap it to strategic partners only. We don't want many small ISVs to expect the same privilege.

Attachments: I sketched a short proposed addendum and a 60-day timeline (proposed-grace-period.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- Hannah: confirm if SageWorks is strategic enough to warrant an exception (I think yes for DEAL-4721).
- Priyom: draft the addendum / procurement language.
- Marcus: provide a short ops runbook and estimate (can you attach by EOD?).

If everyone agrees, I'll draft the reply to Sarah and include the addendum for signature.

—Vanessa
VP, Alliances | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: proposed-grace-period.pdf (PDF, 12 KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@sageworks.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Backcompat exemption for SDK v3 deprecation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear matrix and callout. Appreciate the context.

We can support a short, account-specific grace period for SageWorks while you finish the migration work. Proposed terms: 

- Length: 60 days from 2027-01-15 (new cut date 2027-03-16)
- Requirements: sign the attached one-off addendum committing to the migration target; Redwood will retain v3 metrics for 30 days after cut and reserves the right to force-cut with 14 days notice if stability issues arise.
- Technical plan: we will route SageWorks to a compatibility cluster behind a feature flag; Marcus will share an ops runbook and run-cost estimate separately.

Next steps: please confirm you can commit to the 2027-03-16 migration date and sign the addendum. Vanessa has attached the draft addendum and our proposed timeline. Priyom from procurement/legal is on copy and will follow up about the addendum language.

If you'd prefer a quick call to walk through the risk and staging plan, we're available tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
